item.title: JayQuery: Privacy-Preserving Student Success Prediction
item.description:
JayQuery was ADAL’s SCARP 2026 project on privacy-preserving student success prediction with federated learning.

Colleges are data-rich but insight-poor: FERPA regulations prevent offices such as the Registrar, Financial Aid and the learning management system from merging their student records into a single model. JayQuery uses vertical federated learning (VFL): separate data silos collaborate to train a dropout-risk predictor without ever sharing raw records. The silos align their records through a private set intersection (PSI) handshake, each trains a local “bottom” model, and a federated learning server combines their embeddings in a “top” model protected with differential-privacy noise.

Team

  • Alexander Pellet, system architect and ML engineer
  • Wyatt Wilfong, privacy and security lead
  • Dr. Peilong Li, faculty mentor
